name: William G. Low House

dates.altered: Demolished 1962. Wikipedia: 'Just before it was demolished in 1962, the house was documented with measured drawings and photographs by the Historic American Buildings Survey.'
dates.note: Wikipedia infobox: construction started 1886, completed 1887; the McKim, Mead & White article's table says 1887.

refs.title: William G. Low House - Wikipedia
refs.note: Its own words, quoting Leland Roth: 'Although little known in its own time, the Low House has come to represent the high mark of the Shingle Style.' Location as the infobox prints it: 3 Low Lane, Bristol.

refs.title: McKim, Mead & White - Wikipedia
refs.note: 'The William G. Low House in Bristol, Rhode Island (1886-1887), demolished in 1962, is today seen as a quintessential expression of the Shingle Style', quoting Vincent Scully: 'at once a climax and a kind of conclusion' for McKim.

note: A demolished building, kept as a precedent because the style's own literature (Scully, Roth) names it first and HABS photographed it before the wreckers; there is no register number because it was gone before the Register existed. Seeded 4 Sep 2026.
